perspective:
From Alice Lim’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am a dental hygienist. Austin Moreno is my close friend from high school; we have stayed close and often discuss our personal and professional lives and support each other.
- I know Austin works in insurance/at an office, and our career paths differ.
- I have observed Austin being reserved lately when we talk about work. This made me concerned and curious, and I suspect he may be hiding something about his job performance.
- I invited Austin for coffee to talk about it.
- Austin told me: things at the office are “usual ups and downs”; he is not sure how to handle a few things at work; it is “complicated.”
- I suggested he consider a career change and specifically mentioned healthcare. I offered to share my experiences and connect him with contacts.
- Austin told me he has thought about changing careers but does not know what other paths he could take. He said healthcare sounds interesting and he wants to know more about my experiences and what it involves.
- I sensed Austin was hesitant because of fear of the unknown. I felt both frustration and empathy, and I told him about my friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and is happier.
- Austin told me Lara’s story was inspiring but he worries about risks and the initial struggle.
- I told him it is natural to feel that way, that growth comes from stepping out of our comfort zones, and that I am there to support him.
- Austin thanked me and said it helps to have my support and hear real success stories.
- Seeing his openness, I felt encouraged and hopeful. I offered to help him plan a transition and connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare.
- Austin said that would be helpful and appreciated the connections. I said I would set up a meeting next week. He thanked me and said he was looking forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, I believe Austin is ready to take the next steps and appreciates my help. I feel satisfied and joyful, and I plan regular check-ins with him.
- I told Austin I am proud of the steps he has taken and asked how he feels. He said he feels excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful for my help.
- I suggested regular check-ins. Austin agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that he values my perspective.

I do not have access to Austin’s hidden thoughts, private reasons for being reserved, actual job-performance details, or anything he has not told me. I only have what I observed, what he said, my own actions, and my own beliefs/feelings.
